items.summary: This Notice announces changes in the interest rates to be paid on debentures issued with respect to a loan or mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration under the provisions of the National Housing Act (the Act). The interest rate for debentures issued under Section 221(g)(4) of the Act during the 6-month period beginning July 1, 2026, is 4\1/2\ percent. The interest rate for debentures issued under any other provision of the Act is the rate in effect on the date that the commitment to insure the loan or mortgage was issued, or the date that the loan or mortgage was endorsed (or initially endorsed if there are two or more endorsements) for insurance, whichever rate is higher. The interest rate for debentures issued under these other provisions with respect to a loan or mortgage committed or endorsed during the 6-month period beginning July 1, 2026, is 5 percent.

feature_pitch_raw:
**The pattern:** Inside fifteen days HUD reset the price of three separate federally guaranteed credit programs, and the notices have not been read together. On 09/28/26 the department raised the upfront loan guarantee fee on all new Section 184 firm commitments, stating the increase is meant to keep the program self-sustaining. The same day it announced the Section 108 fee that will cover credit subsidy costs for loans committed in FY 2027. On 10/13/26 it published debenture interest rates for mortgages insured under the National Housing Act, setting the Section 221(g)(4) rate at 4 1/2 percent for the six-month period beginning 07/01/26. The housing cluster behind these items does not hold together as one subject — 14 items, 6 sources, cohesion 0.023 — so the rest of that beat is separate leads. This thread is real: it is the federal cost of borrowing against housing, repriced three times in two weeks, with 13 of those 14 housing items unmatched by any monitored publisher.

**Why it matters:** The parties who pay these fees are borrowers and the projects they finance, which in this sector means multifamily and healthcare properties insured under the National Housing Act, Native borrowers using Section 184, and local governments using Section 108 to fund community facilities. The stake is sized by what the notices actually say: a fee rises, a subsidy cost gets passed through, a debenture rate is fixed for six months. Nobody has published what the three changes do in combination to the cost of financing housing older adults will live in, which means a developer, a tribal housing authority or an older homeowner currently has to read three Federal Register documents to learn what changed about their loan.

**Why pitch this now:** The Section 108 fee applies to commitments awarded in FY 2027, the fiscal year that began 10/01/26, so deals being structured right now are the first affected. The debenture notice carries a 10/13/26 date and fixes a rate through a defined six-month window. The Section 184 increase applies to all new firm commitments rather than to a future cohort.
